title: Nagata rings ascend along weakly etale Noetherian ring maps
statement: Let $A$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Then $B$ is a Nagata ring. No universal catenarity or J-2 assumption is imposed on $A$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Remark 5.7(ii), printed p. 148; Remark 5.2 identifies AF with weakly etale. The proof of Theorem 5.3(iii), printed p. 147, cites [4] for local Nagata ascent; Remark 5.7(ii) records the stronger global Nagata ascent.

proof.text: First establish the field-fibre calculation, for reuse below. Let $k\to F$ be any weakly etale algebra over a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], $F$ is reduced, every finitely generated $k$-subalgebra is finite etale, and its residue fields are separable algebraic over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to the finite subalgebra $k[x]$, for each $x\in F$: every element of $F$ is integral over $k$. For any prime $P$ of $F$, the domain $F/P$ is therefore algebraic over $k$. For $0\ne z\in F/P$, choose a monic relation of least degree. Its constant term is nonzero, since otherwise cancellation of $z$ gives a lower-degree relation. Solving this relation for $z^{-1}$ shows that $F/P$ is a field. Thus every prime of $F$ is maximal, and no two distinct primes are comparable; every prime is also minimal. Now [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] says that $F_P$ is a field for each $P$. In particular these local rings are normal domains by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], because the fraction field of a field is that field itself. Thus $F$ is a normal ring, with every prime maximal, including when $F$ is the zero ring (there are then no primes).

source.place: Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), with algebra.tex Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral) and 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); elementary inverse-polynomial calculation is written out

proof.text: For any weakly etale map $U\to V$ of Noetherian rings and any $U$-algebra $U'$, the ring-to-scheme equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], identified on affine spectra by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], makes $U'\to V\otimes_U U'$ weakly etale. In particular its fibre at $p\subset U$ is $F_p=V\otimes_U\kappa(p)=(U\setminus p)^{-1}(V/pV)$. This ring is Noetherian: $V/pV$ is a cyclic finite $V$-algebra, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] applies, and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] applies. Step 1 shows that every $F_p$ is normal and has all primes maximal. Its residue fields are separable algebraic over $\kappa(p)$. For $q\subset V$ over $p$, the fibre prime is the extension of $q/pV$; its residue field is $\operatorname{Frac}(V/q)=\kappa(q)$: localizing $V/q$ first at $U\setminus p$ and then at all its nonzero elements gives exactly the same fractions as localizing at all nonzero elements at once. Thus $\kappa(q)/\kappa(p)$ is algebraic, including when it is infinite.

source.place: Tag 094U (lemma-base-change-weakly-etale); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence). Fibre fractions are displayed explicitly

proof.text: Fix a prime $q\subset B$, put $p=f^{-1}(q)$, $k=\kappa(p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/p)$ and $E=\kappa(q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/q)$, and fix an arbitrary finite field extension $L/E$. Step 2 gives that $E/k$ is algebraic. There is a finite subextension $L_0/k$ inside $L$ with $L=EL_0$: choose a finite $E$-basis $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $L$. Each $x_i$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $E$; the finitely many coefficients of these polynomials lie in a finite extension $k_1/k$ inside $E$, because adjoining finitely many algebraic elements is spanned successively by bounded powers. The ring $k_1[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is finite dimensional over $k_1$ by the same bounded-power spanning argument and is a domain, hence a field: multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space and is surjective. It is therefore a finite extension of $k$, and so is its subfield $L_0=k(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Finally $EL_0=L$ since $EL_0$ contains the chosen $E$-basis. No finite degree for $E/k$ is asserted.

source.place: Elementary finite field model: choose equations for a finite E-basis, adjoin their algebraic coefficients over k, and use the bounded monomials to obtain a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field. This is the finite-normalization model argument, with no J-2 hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $R\subset L_0$ be the integral closure of $A/p$ in $L_0$. Since $A$ is Nagata, [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] gives that $A/p$ is Japanese; [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] gives that $R$ is finite over $A/p$, hence over $A$. The precise normalization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] gives that $R$ is a normal domain with fraction field $L_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], each prime localization of $R$ is a normal domain, so $R$ is a normal ring as required by the normality ascent lemma.

source.place: Tags 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N), 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); fraction-field clause from the cited existing normalization node

proof.text: Set $C=B\otimes_A R$. Step 2 gives that $R\to C$ is weakly etale. If $r_1,\ldots,r_s$ generate $R$ as an $A$-module, the elements $1\otimes r_j$ generate $C$ as a $B$-module, by expanding each pure tensor and then each sum of pure tensors. Thus $C$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. Its fibre rings over $R$ are normal by step 2; the map $R\to C$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. All five hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] are now present: $R,C$ Noetherian, flatness, normal fibres, and $R$ normal. Consequently $C$ is normal.

source.place: Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian); the finite base-change spanning calculation is written out

proof.text: The maps $B\to B/q\subset E\subset L$ and $R\subset L_0\subset L$ agree on $A$ and give $h:C\to L$, $b\otimes r\mapsto\bar b r$. Write $Q=\ker h$ and $D=h(C)=C/Q\subset L$. Then $Q\cap R=0$ and $Q\cap B=q$. The prime $Q$ is minimal: the generic fibre is weakly etale over $L_0$ by step 2; applying [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] and the algebraic-domain inverse calculation of step 1 shows that all its primes are maximal, so the following extension-contraction argument applies. If $Q_0\subseteq Q$ is another prime of $C$, both avoid every nonzero element of $R$. Their extensions in $C\otimes_R L_0$ are primes, since the quotients embed in localizations of the domains $C/Q_i$. These extensions contract back to $Q_i$: if $sc\in Q_i$ with $0\ne s\in R$, primality gives $c\in Q_i$. But the generic fibre $C\otimes_R L_0$ has every prime maximal by step 2. The two extended primes, one contained in the other, must be equal, hence $Q_0=Q$. This proves minimality without claiming that $h$ is surjective onto $L$.

source.place: Agent prime-ideal calculation from the zero-dimensional generic fibre established in step 2; compare Tag 092Q

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], $C$ has finitely many minimal primes. It is reduced, since every prime localization of the normal ring $C$ is a domain and the maps to those localizations are jointly injective by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] to obtain $C\cong\prod_{i=1}^t C_i$ with each $C_i$ a normal domain. A prime in a finite product chooses one factor: of the orthogonal idempotents $e_i$ summing to $1$, exactly one is outside a prime; all other factors vanish in the quotient. Since $Q$ is minimal, its prime in the selected domain factor is $(0)$. Thus $D=C/Q$ is that normal domain factor. It is finite over $B/q$, generated by the images of $1\otimes r_j$. Its fraction field inside $L$ contains $E$ because it contains $B/q$, and contains $L_0$ because it contains $R$. It therefore equals $EL_0=L$.

source.place: Tags 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components) and 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), together with the source of lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective; product-prime and fraction-field identifications are written out

proof.text: The finite algebra $D$ is integral over $B/q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Conversely any $x\in L$ integral over $B/q$ satisfies the same monic polynomial over the larger subring $D$, so lies in $D$, since $D$ is normal with fraction field $L$. Therefore $D$ is exactly the integral closure of $B/q$ in $L$, and it is finite over $B/q$. The prime $q$ and finite extension $L/E$ were arbitrary. By [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] every $B/q$ is Japanese. With the assumed Noetherianity of $B$, [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] gives that $B$ is Nagata. This part of the argument has not needed J-2. If $B$ is the zero ring there is no prime $q$, so the Japanese conditions are vacuous and its assumed Noetherianity still gives the conclusion.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 032F (definition-N), 032R (definition-nagata); equality with the integral closure is proved in the step

proof_origin.place: Nagata ascent argument reconstructed from Greco, Theorem 5.3(iii) and Remark 5.7(ii), with the finite-normalization construction expanded from Stacks Tags 032R, 032F, 034L, 00FN, 00GY, 00FR and 030C. The shared checkout has no local Stacks sources; the second reader checked the upstream Stacks .tex files directly (see report.md).

split_report.summary: Expanded the Nagata-ascent argument into eight complete steps. The route constructs finite normalizations after passing to residue fields, uses weak-etale field fibres and flat normal-fibre ascent to identify the integral closure, and concludes the Nagata condition for every prime quotient of B. The existing J-2 argument was intentionally omitted because it is not part of this item; no new support nodes were needed.
